explanation: Binary-search the value bounds using prefix counts. Count all entries at most middle; if this exceeds middle, keep the lower value bounds, otherwise move the lower bound above middle. Read the original array without sorting or changing it.
correctness: Maintain an overfull prefix ending at upper and a non-overfull prefix ending at lower-1. Initially the first contains n+1 entries for n possible values and the empty prefix contains zero. The count comparison preserves these bounds. When lower equals upper, subtracting the two prefix counts shows that this single value occurs at least twice.
walkthrough: For [1,3,4,2,3], start with bounds 1..4. At middle 2, exactly two entries are at most 2, so move lower to 3. At middle 3, four entries are at most 3, exceeding three available prefix values, so upper becomes 3. Return 3, leaving the input unchanged.
